Codex review: needs maintainer review before merge. ## What this changes This PR opens desktop rail agent, profile, and Inbox menus beside their controls with an eight-pixel gap. **Example:** Open the agent menu in the 1280 × 900 desktop Control UI. - **Before:** The menu starts at x=8 and covers nearby rail controls. - **After:** The menu starts at x=60, eight pixels beyond the rail, leaving its controls visible. ## Review scores | Measure | Result | What it means | |---|---|---| | **Overall readiness** | 🦐 gold shrimp **(3/6)** | Strong proof and a clean focused patch; the overall tier reflects partial delivery of the linked umbrella issue, whose remaining refinements are intentionally separate. | | **Proof confidence** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** ✨ media proof bonus | Sufficient (screenshot): Inspected before/after screenshots exercise the real Control UI's agent, profile, and Inbox presentation owners with synthetic Gateway data and show each panel clear of the desktop rail; browser coverage supports alignment and Escape focus return in Chromium and WebKit. | | **Patch quality** | 🦞 diamond lobster **(5/6)** | No actionable review findings were identified. | ## Product **Kind:** Bug fix · **Worth it:** Yes · **Fix scope:** Partial **User problem:** Opening desktop rail menus obscures nearby navigation controls. **Reason:** The maintainer-authored PR and linked issue authorize this independent placement refinement; the broader issue intentionally retains two other workstreams. ## Merge readiness ✅ **Ready for maintainer review** Keep this PR open: it delivers a useful, maintainer-directed placement fix with convincing visual evidence, green exact-head checks, and no actionable findings. **Priority:** P3 **Reviewed head:** `d13fad3f4981fa6ba820dea075a7c24c73904f77` ## Before merge None. ## Findings None.
Agent review details ### How this fits together Sidebar presentation owners receive trigger geometry and layout context, then pass placement to the shared native menu primitive or the existing Inbox panel renderer. ```mermaid flowchart LR A[Rail controls] --> B[Sidebar menu owner] A --> C[Inbox presentation owner] B --> D[Shared native menu] C --> E[Inbox panel renderer] D --> F[Positioned panels and focus return] E --> F ``` ### Technical review Best possible solution: Land the focused menu-placement change through the existing presentation owners while retaining the remaining navigation refinements in the linked issue. Do we have a high-confidence way to reproduce the issue? Current-main placement code and the inspected before screenshots establish the overlap path; the contributor also reports a browser regression failing on the base, which this read-only review did not rerun. Is this the best way to solve the issue? The change is appropriately small: existing owners select rail placement, the native primitive supplies positioning and focus behavior, and Inbox retains its viewport clamp. AGENTS.md: found and applied where relevant. Codex review notes: model internal, reasoning medium; reviewed against [aae640af4fdd](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/aae640af4fdd84ed7533f8a1ffc4f24f807ef156). ### Provenance checked - `Agent and profile positioning` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (12c556d669959c3fb5a5c0a0fd88c7ccb6f2badb: The Solid-state refactor carried forward vertical placement; https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/113719 documents the earlier purpose of keeping the agent card visible. This PR explains the rail-specific side placement and preserves the other layouts.) - `Shared native menu adapter` keeps the original intent (f3e38df873ad6ea567c6cd2829ddb80a6b8b2b5e: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/171463 centralized native positioning, dismissal, and return focus; this PR uses that same primitive's existing side placements.) - `Inbox positioning` changes intended behavior with a stated reason (e80558a4da0f3577bc750c5994fdc9f66d35a773: The Solid sidebar migration preserved the existing Inbox presentation; this PR explains the desktop rail exception while retaining non-rail positioning, mobile styling, and viewport clamping.) - `Existing mobile positioning expectations` keeps the original intent (6d1dd21f7668167c8fdd594b6bbd8872537d0f59: The earlier test consolidation preserved positioning contracts; this PR retains their expected coordinates and mounts the actual mobile layout class.) ### Testing Proof path: shipped entry point. ### Security None. ### Evidence What I checked: - **Verified PR scope:** The pinned introduction diff changes rail placement, carries placement through existing menu types, and adds browser regression coverage without introducing another menu owner. ([`ui/src/components/sidebar-menus.tsx:252`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d13fad3f4981fa6ba820dea075a7c24c73904f77/ui/src/components/sidebar-menus.tsx#L252), [d13fad3f4981](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d13fad3f4981fa6ba820dea075a7c24c73904f77)) - **Current main still needs the placement change:** Fetched main still positions the agent menu below its trigger, the profile menu above it, and Inbox around its horizontal center. ([`ui/src/components/sidebar-menus.tsx:249`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/aae640af4fdd84ed7533f8a1ffc4f24f807ef156/ui/src/components/sidebar-menus.tsx#L249), [aae640af4fdd](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/aae640af4fdd84ed7533f8a1ffc4f24f807ef156)) - **Inspected visual proof:** Inspected all three before/after pairs from the running Control UI with synthetic Gateway content: agent, profile, and Inbox move clear of the rail. The Inbox images omitted from local preparation were retrieved and inspected directly. See the [agent result](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/406685ce-4742-4880-ac81-2d4582d3ba12), [profile result](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/99b66a6b-adf4-47d6-ba2c-ac8951313c6c), and [Inbox result](https://github.com/user-attachments/assets/40b6d0b5-aa15-4ab0-833d-751264a5fa07). ([d13fad3f4981](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d13fad3f4981fa6ba820dea075a7c24c73904f77)) - **Consumer-level regression:** The browser test opens all three real sidebar surfaces, checks rail separation and alignment, and verifies Escape returns focus to each original trigger; the body reports failure on the unchanged base and passes in Chromium and WebKit. ([`ui/src/components/app-sidebar-rail-menus.browser.test.ts:19`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/blob/d13fad3f4981fa6ba820dea075a7c24c73904f77/ui/src/components/app-sidebar-rail-menus.browser.test.ts#L19), [d13fad3f4981](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d13fad3f4981fa6ba820dea075a7c24c73904f77)) - **Exact-head checks and merge state:** Live REST reads confirm the reviewed head is open, ready for review, and mergeable with clean merge state; openclaw/ci-gate, UI shards, UI E2E, production types, test types, and status contexts passed. ([d13fad3f4981](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/d13fad3f4981fa6ba820dea075a7c24c73904f77)) - **Approved scope and remaining umbrella work:** The maintainer-authored direction in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/179107 explicitly splits menu placement from surface and control refinements; this PR correctly uses Related and implements the menu slice. Likely related people: - **Peter Steinberger:** Raw commit 12c556d669959c3fb5a5c0a0fd88c7ccb6f2badb adds ui/src/components/sidebar-menus.tsx:218 relative to its recorded parents.
